cookiesPolicy.title: Cookies Policy
cookiesPolicy.intro:
This Cookies Policy explains how DYNAMIA INTELLIGENCE PTE. LTD. uses cookies and similar technologies on https://dynamia.ai/.

We use necessary cookies to operate the Site. Optional categories, including analytics, marketing, and functional cookies, are disabled by default and are used only after you provide consent through our cookie banner or preferences panel.

You can change your choices at any time by opening Cookie Settings in the footer.

sections.title: What are cookies?
sections.content:
Cookies are small text files consisting solely of letters and numbers. A web server places them on your computer or mobile device when you visit a webpage. Cookies can enhance the user - friendliness of our Services, for instance, by remembering your language preferences and settings. For more details about cookies, visit www.allaboutcookies.org.

Cookies are extensively used to make websites function efficiently. They allow you to navigate between pages smoothly, remember your preferences, and make your interaction with the Services more seamless and efficient. Cookies also help ensure that the online advertisements you see are relevant to you and your interests.

sections.title: Cookie categories we use
sections.content:
Necessary: required for core site behavior such as language routing, remembering your cookie consent choice, and maintaining limited access state for gated video content.

Analytics: used only with consent to understand traffic and performance through Google Analytics, Baidu Analytics, Vercel Analytics, and Vercel Speed Insights.

Marketing: reserved for campaign measurement, advertising, or remarketing. We do not enable marketing cookies unless you opt in.

Functional: reserved for optional experience preferences beyond what is strictly required. We do not enable functional cookies unless you opt in.

sections.title: Current cookies and similar technologies

Google Analytics (_ga and related cookies): third-party analytics cookies used only after analytics consent. Retention is controlled by Google Analytics settings.

Baidu Analytics (Hm_ and related cookies): used to measure traffic sources and page visits only after analytics consent. Data is processed by Baidu; retention is controlled by Baidu Analytics settings.

Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights: analytics and performance measurement technologies used only after analytics consent. Retention is controlled by Vercel.

sections.title: Your choices regarding cookies

You can accept all optional categories, reject all optional categories, or manage individual categories through our cookie banner. You can change your decision later by selecting Cookie Settings in the footer.

You may also restrict or block cookies through your browser settings. Blocking necessary cookies may affect site behavior.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about Dynamia AI and our heterogeneous computing platform.

questions.question: What is Dynamia AI?
questions.answer: Dynamia AI is an enterprise-grade heterogeneous computing platform built on HAMi technology. It provides GPU sharing, auto-scaling, and unified management for AI workloads, enabling organizations to maximize their computing resource utilization.

questions.question: What is HAMi?
questions.answer: HAMi (Heterogeneous AI Computing Middleware) is an open-source project and CNCF Incubating project that provides GPU virtualization and resource management capabilities. It is the core technology behind Dynamia AI's enterprise platform.

questions.question: How does GPU sharing work?
questions.answer: Dynamia AI dynamically consolidates and orchestrates GPU resources, allowing multiple workloads to share GPU memory and compute resources efficiently. This eliminates waste, maximizes resource utilization, and reduces operational costs.

questions.question: What types of workloads does Dynamia AI support?
questions.answer: Dynamia AI supports AI/ML training and inference, high-performance computing (HPC), edge computing, and various other computational workloads that require GPU acceleration.

questions.question: Is Dynamia AI compatible with Kubernetes?
questions.answer: Yes, Dynamia AI is built for Kubernetes environments and integrates seamlessly with existing Kubernetes clusters. It provides enhanced scheduling and resource management capabilities on top of Kubernetes.

questions.question: How is pricing determined?
questions.answer: Dynamia AI offers flexible pricing based on your cluster size, number of nodes, and GPU count. We provide customized pricing plans that scale with your infrastructure needs. Contact us for a detailed quote.

questions.question: What support is included?
questions.answer: Enterprise customers receive professional technical support, including setup assistance, troubleshooting, best practices guidance, and continuous updates and maintenance.

questions.question: Can I try Dynamia AI before purchasing?
questions.answer: Yes, we offer free trials for qualified organizations. You can apply for a trial through our website to evaluate Dynamia AI in your environment before making a commitment.

gpuCatalog.title: Heterogeneous GPU compatibility
gpuCatalog.description: Explore supported NVIDIA, AMD, AWS and Chinese accelerators, including device families, resource-sharing capabilities and deployment requirements.
gpuCatalog.empty: No matching model. Contact our team to confirm compatibility.
gpuCatalog.boundaryText: Tell us about your GPU models, cluster environment and workloads. Together, we can find the right approach to resource sharing, scheduling and management.
gpuCatalog.name: Vendor

devices.name: NVIDIA
devices.detail: Supports memory and compute sharing, isolation, multi-GPU virtualization and Binpack / Spread scheduling. Requires drivers compatible with the GPU and CUDA, NVIDIA Container Toolkit and the HAMi device plugin. Disable GPU Operator’s native device plugin when using it.

devices.name: AMD
devices.detail: Supports concurrent GPU sharing, memory allocation in MiB and proportional compute-unit (CU) allocation. Requires AMD drivers, ROCm and the HAMi AMD device plugin. Shared workloads need glibc 2.34 or later; disable AMD GPU Operator’s native device plugin.

devices.name: AWS
devices.detail: Supports NeuronCore-based resource allocation, device sharing and topology-aware multi-device scheduling for training and inference. Deploy on Inf / Trn EC2 instances with Neuron drivers and runtime, Neuron Device Plugin and HAMi.

devices.name: Huawei Ascend
devices.detail: Template-based hardware partitioning or software sharing. Memory and compute capabilities depend on the mode; software sharing requires compatible ARM hardware, drivers and the HAMi scheduler.

devices.name: Hygon
devices.detail: Memory and compute sharing; memory isolation is model-dependent. Requires the vendor device plugin and compatible DTK/drivers. Check the single-container vDCU limit.

devices.name: Cambricon
devices.detail: Memory and compute sharing. The MLU370 guide requires Dynamic SMLU and matching drivers/CNToolkit; verify the applicable versions for other models.

devices.name: MetaX
devices.detail: Memory and compute sharing via sGPU. Enable vendor virtualization and install the device plugin for the specific model.

devices.name: Iluvatar CoreX
devices.detail: Memory and compute sharing; the guide specifies 256 MiB memory and 1% compute granularity. Requires GPU Manager and compatible drivers; verify device limits per container.

devices.name: Moore Threads
devices.detail: Memory and compute sharing. Partition granularity and isolation depend on the vendor driver and deployment guide.

devices.name: Kunlunxin
devices.detail: Whole-device scheduling and a VXPU path. Memory sharing does not imply independent compute partitioning. Whole-device scheduling is topology-aware; select the deployment mode explicitly.

devices.name: Enflame
devices.detail: Memory and compute sharing. Allocate resources using supported vGCU/device-plugin configurations; verify driver and device mode.

devices.name: Vastai
devices.detail: Listed as schedulable in the public matrix, without memory or compute partitioning. Plan for whole-device allocation and confirm any sharing requirements separately.

devices.name: Biren
devices.detail: Listed as schedulable in the public matrix, without memory or compute partitioning. Confirm the model, plugin and delivery scope for the target environment.

devices.name: T-Head
devices.detail: Supports fine-grained memory and compute isolation within unified compute management. Integrates through the Dynamia PPU device plugin with Zhenwu drivers, runtime and Dynamia product components.

why.title: Why choose Dynamia
why.description: From resource efficiency to unified management, make every GPU count.

panels.label: Heterogeneous clusters
panels.title: Bring distributed compute into one view
panels.body: Connect public cloud, private cloud and on-premises Kubernetes clusters to view nodes, devices and workloads together. Resource pools and team permissions define clear usage boundaries.

panels.label: GPU sharing
panels.title: One GPU. Multiple workloads.
panels.body: Request GPU memory, compute capacity and device counts according to each task. Place multiple workloads on suitable GPUs to reduce idle resources caused by full-device allocation.

panels.label: GPU oversubscription
panels.title: Use host memory for flexible GPU memory demand
panels.body: Manage workload memory across GPU and host memory to enable oversubscription for suitable workloads. Validate actual gains and latency against the model and access patterns.

panels.label: Dynamic scaling
panels.title: Adjust GPU memory quotas as demand changes
panels.body: Within available capacity, automatically expand or manually resize GPU memory quotas for running containers, reducing the need to recreate containers when memory settings change.

panels.label: Centralized observability
panels.title: Trace resource use from cluster to workload
panels.body: Combine Kubernetes status and Prometheus metrics to view device utilization, GPU memory, workload status and historical trends for capacity analysis and troubleshooting.

panels.label: Advanced AI scheduling
panels.title: Align resource allocation with your policies
panels.body: Use Binpack, Spread, device model and UUID selection, and topology-aware policies to balance packing, load distribution and workload communication needs.

community.leadAfter: and continue to drive its development. We are building the open-source core of AI infrastructure to make heterogeneous compute easier to use, more efficient and easier to govern.

items.q: Is HAMi open source? How does it relate to Dynamia’s products?
items.a: HAMi is a CNCF Incubating project. Dynamia is its leading initiator and ongoing driving force, building the open-source core of AI infrastructure to make heterogeneous compute easier to use, more efficient and easier to govern.

items.q: Which product fits an existing Kubernetes or custom platform?
items.a: If you already run Kubernetes or PaaS and need GPU virtualization and scheduling, start with Dynamia Enterprise for HAMi. For visual multi-cluster, tenant, quota and usage management, explore Dynamia AI Platform for HAMi.

items.q: Which GPUs are supported? Do all devices offer the same capabilities?
items.a: The accelerator ecosystem on this page lists integrated vendors. Specific capabilities depend on the device model, drivers, software stack and product version. Validate sharing, isolation and monitoring individually. Share your device inventory so our team can confirm compatibility.

items.q: Does GPU sharing affect application performance?
items.a: Performance depends on workload type, resource quotas, concurrency and hardware. Compare throughput, latency, GPU memory and GPU utilization with representative workloads before choosing a production configuration.

items.q: Where can I find real-world case studies?
items.a: Our Case studies page brings together user experience across different business scenarios, including context, technical approaches and key outcomes. Results apply to each case’s stated environment and measurement scope.

items.q: What should I prepare for a product evaluation?
items.a: Prepare GPU models and counts, cluster and software versions, representative workloads and target metrics. Use “Book a demo” below to discuss validation scope and evaluation methods with our team.

items.q: How can I join the community or contact Dynamia?
items.a: Visit our Community page to learn about HAMi and join open-source discussions. For enterprise products, book a demo, email info@dynamia.ai or call 400-026-7800.

hami.name: HAMi
hami.body1: HAMi is open-source middleware for heterogeneous GPU virtualization and sharing. Its lightweight, non-intrusive deployment works across public, private and hybrid clouds, enabling flexible, reliable, on-demand GPU sharing.
hami.body2: HAMi improves device utilization through GPU memory and compute sharing, resource isolation and scheduling. It supports heterogeneous chips including NVIDIA, Ascend, MetaX, Cambricon, Hygon, Moore Threads and Iluvatar CoreX, integrating with existing Kubernetes infrastructure.

story.line1: Dynamia was founded by the creators and core maintainers of HAMi, a CNCF Incubating project, with a mission to build the open-source core of AI infrastructure. Through open-source collaboration, we develop the underlying scheduling and virtualization capabilities for heterogeneous compute, making GPUs and other AI accelerators easier to use, more efficient and easier to govern in cloud-native environments. Focused on heterogeneous GPU resource virtualization, efficient scheduling and production deployment, Dynamia helps enterprises turn fragmented, complex and costly compute resources into infrastructure that can be shared, isolated and consumed on demand.
story.line2: HAMi is currently the only open-source project in the industry dedicated to heterogeneous GPU resource virtualization and efficient scheduling. It improves resource utilization through flexible, reliable, on-demand and elastic GPU virtualization, with lightweight, pluggable and non-intrusive deployment across public, private and hybrid clouds. HAMi supports mainstream GPU and accelerator providers including NVIDIA, AMD and AWS, and integrates seamlessly with upstream and downstream open-source schedulers such as Volcano, Koordinator, Kueue and KAI Scheduler, steadily building a reliable heterogeneous compute ecosystem.
